terms.meaning: Provider secures the underlying cloud; the customer secures what they deploy and configure on it.

spec.as: The provider secures the cloud; you secure what you put in it.

terms.meaning: AWS wording of the split: AWS owns Security "of" the Cloud, the customer Security "in" the Cloud.
Service models defined in NIST SP 800-145 (2011); the customer's security share shrinks toward SaaS.
How far one compromised identity, key or account can reach; guardrails exist to shrink it.

spec.as: Design so one stolen key can only burn a small part of it.

terms.meaning: Identity and Access Management: who can do what to which cloud resource, under which conditions.
Instance Metadata Service: per-VM endpoint that serves configuration and temporary role credentials.
Session-oriented IMDSv2 is preferred over request/response IMDSv1; Security Hub CSPM EC2.8 checks for it.
High-profile cloud breach that ATT&CK cites as a metadata API abuse case under T1552.005.
The emblematic cloud leak: object storage anyone can read. Security Hub CSPM S3.2 flags public read.
CIDR for any IPv4 address; as an SSH ingress source it fails Security Hub CSPM EC2.13.
Cloud Security Posture Management: continuous checks of cloud configuration against benchmarks and policy.
Cloud Native Application Protection Platform: one platform unifying CSPM, CWPP and code-to-cloud checks.
Numeronym for Kubernetes: K, eight letters, s. The container orchestrator everyone has to secure.
Role-Based Access Control: Kubernetes authorizes API verbs on resources via Roles and RoleBindings.
Default Kubernetes ClusterRole allowing super-user access to any action on any resource.
PodSecurityPolicy, deprecated in v1.21 and removed in v1.25, gave way to built-in Pod Security Admission.
Container setting that disables most security mechanisms; the Baseline Pod Security Standard disallows it.
Key-value store holding all Kubernetes cluster state, Secrets included; default ports 2379-2380.
Reminder that Kubernetes Secrets are stored unencrypted in etcd by default; turn on encryption at rest.
Infrastructure as Code: cloud resources declared in files and reviewed, versioned and scanned like code.
Guardrails written as versioned, testable rules (Rego, CEL) and enforced automatically in pipelines.

spec.as: Write the guardrail once as code, then check every deploy.

terms.meaning: CIS Amazon Web Services Foundations Benchmark: baseline account hardening checks.
CIS Kubernetes Benchmark: hardening checks for control plane, worker nodes and policies.
Azure Active Directory was renamed Microsoft Entra ID (announced July 11, 2023); capabilities unchanged.

galley.as: for Azure AD read Microsoft Entra ID

terms.meaning: Default kubeconfig kubectl reads: clusters, users and credentials. Guard it like a key.
Local file where the AWS CLI stores profile credentials; short-lived sessions beat stored keys.
Hijacking cloud compute to mine cryptocurrency; ATT&CK Resource Hijacking: Compute Hijacking.
AWS API activity log; CloudTrail.1 wants a multi-Region trail with read and write management events.
The all-powerful account owner identity: MFA on, no access keys (Security Hub CSPM IAM.4), used rarely.
Region code for AWS US East (N. Virginia); the default in countless examples and outage jokes.
Jargon for changing cloud resources by hand in the console instead of through reviewed IaC.
Gap between the IaC-declared state and what actually runs; detect it, then reconcile or codify.
Emergency admin identity kept sealed and closely monitored, used only when normal access fails.

spec.as: Keep one emergency account sealed, alarmed and rarely used.

terms.meaning: CNAPP jargon: individually moderate risks on one asset that together open a critical attack path.
IAM permission to hand a role to an AWS service; a key checkpoint in any privilege review.
Current IAM policy language version; 2008-10-17 is the older one and lacks policy variables.
Wildcard principal in a resource policy: with no limiting Condition it means anyone. Reviewers strike it first.
In IAM evaluation an explicit deny overrides any allow; the guardrail line reviewers insert.
AWS Organizations guardrails: SCPs cap what principals can do; RCPs (Nov 2024) cap access to resources.
Swap an external OIDC token for short-lived cloud credentials, so no static keys are stored.
AWS access key ID prefixes: AKIA marks a long-term access key, ASIA a temporary STS key.
EC2 metadata option that turns IMDSv1 off and requires IMDSv2 session tokens.
IMDSv2 hop limit AWS recommends when containers on the instance need metadata access.
ATT&CK sub-technique of Unsecured Credentials: credentials exposed via the metadata service.
Beta GKE node metadata filter, superseded: Google says use Workload Identity Federation for GKE.
ATT&CK Valid Accounts: Cloud Accounts, where stolen or misused cloud identities are the way in.
ATT&CK technique for collecting data from cloud object storage.
ATT&CK technique for breaking out of a container onto the underlying node.
Cloud log tampering moved to Defense Impairment (TA0112) under a new ID in ATT&CK v19.
ATT&CK technique: activity in regions an org never uses, where monitoring is often thinner.
ATT&CK group that has primarily targeted cloud and container environments to deploy cryptominers.
Kubernetes group bound to cluster-admin by the default bindings: super-user by membership.
The three Pod Security Standards profiles, from unrestricted to heavily hardened.
Short for the Pod Security Admission enforce label set to restricted: failing pods are rejected.
securityContext field the Restricted profile requires: containers must not run as root.
Pod or ServiceAccount field that stops Kubernetes from auto-injecting API credentials.
In-tree Kubernetes admission policy written in CEL; stable since v1.30.
Default TCP port of the kubelet API on every node; it should never face the internet.
Short-lived, auto-rotating TokenRequest token; since v1.22 it replaces static Secret-based tokens in pods.

terms.text: K08: Cluster To Cloud Lateral Movement
terms.meaning: OWASP Kubernetes Top 10 (2025 edition) risk: pivoting from a cluster into the surrounding cloud account.
kube-apiserver flaw in proxied upgrade request handling; CVSS 9.8, fixed in v1.10.11, v1.11.5, v1.12.3.
ingress-nginx admission controller flaw reachable from the pod network; CVSS 9.8, published March 2025.
Remote code execution in Open Management Infrastructure (OMI), an agent used by Azure VM extensions; CVSS 9.8.
Cloud Workload Protection Platform: runtime protection for VMs, containers and serverless.
Cloud Infrastructure Entitlement Management: finds unused and excessive cloud permissions. Not SIEM.
Security Hub CSPM finding workflow statuses: the review state, separate from the compliance result.
Security Hub CSPM control: EC2 instances should use Instance Metadata Service Version 2 (IMDSv2).
Security Hub CSPM: S3 general purpose buckets should have block public access settings enabled (account-level).
Security Hub CSPM control: IAM root user access key should not exist.
Terraform's default local state file; it can hold sensitive values, so keep it in a secured backend.
Aqua folded tfsec's Terraform scanning into Trivy and encourages the community to migrate.
Open-source static analysis scanner for IaC such as Terraform, CloudFormation and Kubernetes manifests.
Open-source tool that checks a cluster against the CIS Kubernetes Benchmark.
CIS benchmark for baseline Microsoft Azure hardening.
Cloud Security Alliance Cloud Controls Matrix: 207 controls across 17 security domains.
NIST Application Container Security Guide (September 2017): container risks and countermeasures.
ISO/IEC standard of information security controls for cloud services, built on ISO/IEC 27002.
One of four S3 Block Public Access settings: calls that set a public ACL on a bucket or object fail.
Legacy Google Cloud org policy constraint blocking service account keys; Google recommends iam.managed.* instead.
AWS Well-Architected security principle: reduce or remove direct human access to data, lowering the risk of mishandling.
AWS Well-Architected security principle: monitor, alert on and audit actions in real time (once 'Enable traceability').
AWS Well-Architected security principle: defense in depth from the network edge down to the application code.
AWS Well-Architected security principle: have incident management, run response drills, automate detection and recovery.
AWS culture maxim: security comes before any number-one priority. AWS repeats it across its blogs and talks.
Security Hub compliance status for a check that could not run: an outage, an API error or an AWS Config NOT_APPLICABLE.
The IAM default: a request that no policy statement allows is denied, and no statement has to say so.
The error code an S3 request gets when the caller is not allowed to perform the action.
The error code an S3 request gets when the named bucket does not exist.
Latin digit 0 and capital O look the same in most fonts; Unicode UTS #39 lists them as confusable.
Latin e and Cyrillic ie look the same in most fonts; Unicode UTS #39 lists them as confusable (lookalike names).
Latin digit 1 and l look the same in most fonts; Unicode UTS #39 lists them as confusable.
Latin a and Cyrillic a look the same in most fonts; Unicode UTS #39 lists them as confusable.
Latin o and Cyrillic o look the same in most fonts; Unicode UTS #39 lists them as confusable.
Known-answer test: a Kubernetes Secret stores its values base64-encoded, not encrypted; "admin" reads YWRtaW4=.

terms.text: S3 ETag of an empty object
terms.meaning: Known-answer test: a single-part upload's ETag is the MD5 of its content; here zero bytes, first 96 bits.
Known-answer test: SHA-256 of zero bytes, the hash of an empty file or empty request body; first 96 bits shown.
AWS STS action that returns temporary credentials for an IAM role; the role's trust policy says who may call it.
AWS threat detection service that analyzes CloudTrail events, VPC flow logs and DNS logs for suspicious activity.
AWS service that correlates signals from GuardDuty, Inspector, Macie and Security Hub CSPM to rank security risks.
Open-source cloud security tool that audits AWS, Azure, GCP and Kubernetes against built-in checks and benchmarks.
Open-source runtime security tool for hosts, containers and Kubernetes; rules over kernel events raise alerts.
OPA is a policy engine with the Rego language; Gatekeeper applies it as a Kubernetes admission webhook.
Kubernetes object that sets which Pod traffic is allowed, by IP address and port; a network plugin must enforce it.
CIS Google Cloud Platform Foundation Benchmark: secure configuration guidelines for baseline Google Cloud hardening.
IAM policy language versions: AWS says to use 2012-10-17, not the earlier 2008-10-17, in new or updated policies.
Breaking out of a container to reach its host node; ATT&CK calls the technique Escape to Host.
ATT&CK technique: an adversary deploys a container to run code or slip past existing defenses.
